summary: ALB coalescing of multiple Range units in outbound requests causes sharded artifact checksum mismatch
description:
Issue summary:
Customer FinLedger reports intermittent shard validation failures when downloading model artifacts via presigned range GETs from a Private deployment behind their corporate ALB. The presigned GETs return 200 OK, but the assembled shard checksums do not match what the serving node expects, causing runtime checksum-fail aborts and degraded KV-cache warmup.

Impact:
- Serving nodes fail to load model shard(s) intermittently, causing increased cold-start latency and occasional fallbacks to smaller model variants.
- A subset (~2-3%) of shard downloads during nightly batch pulls result in checksum mismatch and abort, impacting capacity and customer SLAs.

Environment:
- Private deployment in customer VPC with a customer-managed application load balancer (ALB) in front of their corporate egress proxy.
- Redwood control plane and presigned URLs hosted in us-east-1.
- Affected nodes attempt concurrent multi-range downloads for shards (client issues 2-range requests per object).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure Private deployment with presigned S3-compatible URLs for shard range downloads.
2) From a host behind customer's ALB + egress proxy, issue parallel GETs with two Range units in the same request (e.g., Range: bytes=0-524287,524288-1048575).
3) Observe 200 responses but computed SHA256 checksum differs from expected on ~1-3% of attempts.
4) Reproduced reliably when traffic is routed through the customer's ALB; not reproducible from other networks.
logs: Serving node logs: shard-fetch failed checksum: expected=ab12... got=9f3c... (partial content mismatch)
S3 access logs: 200 OK returned for presigned GET id=xyz-123, bytes served in two ranges
Customer tcpdump: outbound GET shows single Range header that appears normalized (units merged/reordered) by ALB before egress proxy.
Edge logs: occasional duplicate content-length values observed on 200 responses from upstream egress proxy.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: range-splitting or range-ordering mutation in transit leads to server returning merged byte ranges that client-side assembler misattributes to requested offsets.

Support downloaded pcap from customer — verified original client request contained two properly-formatted range units separated by a comma. Upstream observed request (captured after ALB) shows a single Range header value where units are coalesced and ordering is changed; in some cases spacing/semicolon normalization removed a crucial separator the object store relies on for multipart range processing.
Replayed requests directly to S3 origin from RW support network show correct behavior; replay from customer's ALB reproduces checksum drift.

SRE inspected ALB configuration and found a custom listener rule and a vendor-managed rewrite module (third-party WAF appliance) in front of the egress proxy; that appliance advertises header normalization and canonicalization features.
Correlation: failures cluster to specific ALB instance pool that routes through the third-party WAF/accelerator. Instances bypassing the accelerator show no failures.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:22 - Aisha Patel (Support): Initial report from FinLedger - shard integrity errors starting 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC after a routine shard refresh. Customer provided sample client-side sha256 and tcpdump.

2026-03-10 11:10 - Liam Chen (SRE): Verified mismatch in packets captured before and after ALB. Suspect header rewriter on customer's ALB path. Requested ALB config and VPC flow log for the affected AZ.
2026-03-11 07:45 - FinLedger (Customer): Confirmed they recently enabled a vendor-managed WAF/accelerator rule-set (header canonicalization) last week. They can toggle it off for testing.

2026-03-11 14:02 - Liam Chen (SRE): Customer toggled the accelerator off for a 2-hour window — no checksum mismatches observed during that window. Re-enabled and failures returned. Conclusion: header accelerator is mutating Range headers.

2026-03-12 10:30 - Product Eng (Maya Rodriguez): Observed that some object stores treat comma-separated multi-range requests strictly; a mutated single-string value with missing comma or different separators causes server to return a coalesced byte stream in a different ordering, which breaks client assembler assumptions.
2026-03-12 15:20 - Support (Aisha Patel): Communicated temporary workarounds to customer and scheduled follow-up call with vendor and customer network ops. Recommended permanent fix approaches.
resolution:
Workaround applied: Customer disabled the vendor header-canonicalization feature on the ALB/accelerator for egress to Redwood presigned endpoints. After disabling, shard downloads returned correct checksums and serving node load failures stopped.

Planned permanent remediation: 1) Customer to keep canonicalization disabled for calls to Redwood presigned endpoints and create an allowlist for presigned-hostnames. 2) Support guide updated with recommendation to avoid multi-range presigned GETs through header-normalizing middleboxes — added to runbook. 3) Engineering to add detection and more descriptive logs for checksum mismatches that include observed Range header text for easier triage (tracking PR: gh-rlw/infra#4321).

Follow-ups: Customer network team to engage vendor to patch header normalization behavior to preserve comma separation and ordering for Range headers. Redwood will add a console warning/tip for Private deployments behind ALBs that use vendor accelerators.
next_steps: 1) Customer to confirm vendor engineering ticket and ETA for fix.
2) RW SRE to land log-improvement PR to capture upstream Range header observed text in artifact-fetch traces.
3) Update Private deployment checklist and docs to call out header-normalizing middlebox risk.
